messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: High queue growth detected in gpu-pool-us-west-2 (pools/gpu-ssd-32) — autoscaler failing to add capacity, throttle increasing > 95th pct. Alert: queue_length_spike, autoscaler_errors. Impacting hosted inference latency and queued requests. Notified oncall.
oncall-amber: taking it. digging in now. which customers impacted?
sre-jay: i'll pull cluster state and autoscaler logs. amber, watch for rate limit errors on the API.
runtime-ops: prelim: noticed sudden drop in continuous-batching_hit_rate and a spike in prefix_cache_miss. potential config rollback?
oncall-amber: seeing lots of 429s in edge logs referencing token-throttle. customers reporting slow responses. cs-maya, any inbound tickets?
customer-success-maya: one enterprise customer (acme-inc) raised a support ticket about failing generation jobs ~10m ago. flagged as P1.
eng-oncall-sam: I can help with quick rollback if we identify a rollout. any recent traffic shaping or batch config changes?
ml-infra-lee: we deployed a batching config tweak 12m ago to reduce small-batch latency (continuous_batch.window_ms from 50 -> 20 and prefix_cache.ttl from 10m -> 30s) as part of perf experiment. that could explain higher miss rate.
sre-jay: confirmed in deploy history: change id deploy-2026-03-15-1145 pushed to runtime-batching. autoscaler logs show "scale_request_failed: pool_capacity_limit" starting ~11:48. cluster GPU utilization high but queues keep growing — suggests throughput per-GPU dropped.
runtime-ops: yep, lowering prefix_cache.ttl caused prefix cache thrash and continuous batching window shrink means fewer batch coalesces. net effect: token throughput per-GPU dropped ~30%.
oncall-amber: plan: revert batching config to previous values to restore throughput and trigger autoscaler to catch up. also open a manual scale override to allow extra nodes while we revert. any objections?
eng-oncall-sam: go ahead, i'll stage rollback. rolling back deploy-2026-03-15-1145 -> revert-2026-03-15-1202.
eng-oncall-sam: rollback command:
```
replicated-deploy rollback --service runtime-batching --to deploy-2026-03-15-1130
```
eng-oncall-sam: executing now.
pager-handoff-bot: amber acknowledged incident at 11:52 UTC. sam initiated rollback at 11:54 UTC.
runtime-ops: also submitting manual scale:
```
autoscaler override --pool gpu-ssd-32 --target-instances 6 --duration 10m
```
ml-infra-lee: prefix_cache.ttl set back to 10m and continuous_batch.window_ms -> 50ms in the reverted config.
sre-jay: autoscaler accepted override, nodes provisioning. watching queue size.
oncall-amber: queue length peaked at 18k, now trending down to 7k after nodes provisioned. 429 rate dropping.
customer-success-maya: sent update to acme-inc: "we've identified a batching configuration experiment that increased request queuing; we've reverted and are scaling temporarily; your requests should recover shortly."
eng-oncall-sam: metrics: per-GPU throughput back to expected levels ~8k tokens/s per card; continuous_batch hit_rate rising.
runtime-ops: prefix_cache_hit_ratio back above 90% after warmup.
sre-jay: autoscaler removed override and resumed normal policy at 12:04 UTC, cluster stable.
oncall-amber: marking as mitigated. still tracking customer errors until tail drains. anyone see residual errors?
customer-success-maya: acme-inc confirms success, says jobs resumed normally. happy to mark customer impact resolved.
eng-oncall-sam: quick root cause: experiment reduced cache TTL and batch window -> increased cache misses and smaller batches causing lower GPU throughput; autoscaler saw high utilization and attempted to scale but hit pool max (scale cap) and errors prevented capacity catch-up.
sre-jay: follow-ups: 1) revert experiment from canary until we have more perf sim tests; 2) add autoscaler guard to allow temporary burst overrides when queue spike detected; 3) add perf regression alert on per-GPU throughput correlated with batching change.
oncall-amber: assigning tasks: @eng-oncall-sam to open PR to gate batching experiments with perf canary limits; @ml-infra-lee to add an automated perf test for small-batch throughput; @sre-jay to update runbook with manual override steps and add a check to prevent scale cap blocking.
sre-jay: creating incident doc and scheduling postmortem meeting for 48h.
pager-handoff-bot: incident severity -> S2. pagers released.
oncall-amber: final note: we should also add a runtime health check that fails fast if prefix cache miss rate exceeds threshold for >1m. that would prevent silent throughput degradation.
runtime-ops: filed ticket INF-1324 for runtime healthcheck and INF-1325 for autoscaler temporary-burst policy.
sre-jay: thanks everyone. I'll close this thread after the follow-up items are tracked. :thumbsup:
